rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Past care assures the Prophet that God will not abandon him after raising him from weakness to honor.
rows.anchor: أن اتصاله بما تقدم هو أنه تعالى يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wajada means to know; both accusatives are its objects, so God knew him as an orphan and sheltered him.
rows.anchor: من الوجود الذي بمعنى العلم

rows.speaker: أهل الأخبار
rows.claim: The historians say ʿAbd Allāh died while Muḥammad’s mother was pregnant; she died when he was six, his grandfather two years later, and Abū Ṭālib then raised and supported him.
rows.anchor: عبد الله بن عبد المطلب فيما ذكره أهل الأخبار توفي

rows.speaker: أبو طالب
rows.claim: Abū Ṭālib told al-ʿAbbās he kept Muḥammad constantly close, found him modest and protected, and heard him invoke God at meals; he never saw him lie or join ignorant play.
rows.anchor: قال أبو طالب يوما لأخيه العباس : ألا أخبرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī says reports of the Prophet’s marvels, including the monk Baḥīrā story, are well known.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن العجائب المروية في حقه من حديث بحيرى الراهب وغيره مشهورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes yatīm as a unique pearl: the Prophet had no peer among Quraysh, and Abū Ṭālib was the one with whom he could take refuge.
rows.anchor: أنه من قولهم درة يتيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has fa-awā, meaning either that God sheltered him or showed him mercy.
rows.anchor: وهو على معنيين : إما من أواه بمعنى آواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine reminding strengthens the Prophet and promises lasting favor; Pharaoh’s reminder of raising Moses was blameworthy because it demanded service, while God promises to complete His bounty.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك يحسن إذا قصد بذلك أن يقوي قلبه ويعده بدوام النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī likens abandoning care before completion to losing a fetus: that is condemned and incurs compensation, so how could the Ever-Living Sustainer abandon His care?
rows.anchor: أن الحامل التي تسقط الولد قبل التمام معيبة ترد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He contrasts a community whose fourth member is a dog with Muḥammad’s community, for which God Himself is the fourth.
rows.anchor: في تلك الأمة ،   وفي أمة محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A debt of beneficence is harder to discharge than a financial debt: pardon does not cancel it, it lasts a lifetime, and great gifts are impossible to repay fully.
rows.anchor: الدين نوعان مالي وإنعامي ( والثاني )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response is to shelter orphans, guide people and provide for them as God did; even good works depend on God’s enabling and guidance.
rows.anchor: الطريق إلى ذلك أن تفعل في حق عبيدي ما فعلته في حقك

rows.speaker: بعض الناس
rows.claim: Some say the Prophet was initially an unbeliever, then God guided him and made him a prophet.
rows.anchor: أن بعض الناس ذهب إلى أنه كان كافرا في أول الأمر

rows.speaker: القائلون بذلك
rows.claim: Those alleging prior unbelief cite verses about not knowing Scripture or faith, being among the unaware, and the consequence of associating partners.
rows.anchor: على ذلك بآيات أخر منها قوله

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says he was an unbeliever among a misguided people, then guided to monotheism.
rows.anchor: الكلبي : { وجدك ضالا } يعني كافرا في قوم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says the Prophet followed his people’s religion for forty years.
rows.anchor: السدي : كان على دين قومه أربعين سنة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says he was astray from his religion’s guidance.
rows.anchor: مجاهد : { وجدك ضالا } عن الهدى لدينه

rows.speaker: الجمهور من العلماء
rows.claim: The majority agree that the Prophet never disbelieved in God, even for a moment; Rāzī endorses this conclusion.
rows.anchor: وأما الجمهور من العلماء فقد اتفقوا على أنه عليه السلام ما كفر بالله لحظة واحدة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila consider prior unbelief rationally impossible because it would repel people from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: المعتزلة : هذا غير جائز عقلا لما فيه من التنفير

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Rāzī’s school says it is rationally possible for an unbeliever to receive faith and prophethood, though it did not occur here.
rows.anchor: وعند أصحابنا هذا غير ممتنع عقلا لأنه جائز في العقول أن يكون الشخص كافرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scriptural proof excludes that possibility in the Prophet’s case: his companion neither strayed nor erred.
rows.anchor: هذا الجائز لم يقع وهو قوله تعالى : { ما ضل صاحبكم وما غوى }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك وشهر بن حوشب
rows.claim: They interpret this as being unaware of divine favor and revealed law, then guided to them; they connect it with verses about not knowing Scripture and being among the unaware.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك وشهر بن حوشب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One story says the infant became lost from wet nurse Ḥalīma; at Hubal the idols fell and a voice foretold their destruction by the child.
rows.anchor: ضل عن مرضعته حليمة حين أرادت أن ترده إلى جده

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says he was lost as a small child from his grandfather ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, nearly died of hunger, and was guided back; a camel moved only when he sat in front.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : «ضللت عن جدي عبد المطلب وأنا صبي ضائع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God returned him to his grandfather through an enemy’s hand, as Moses was preserved through his enemy.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس : رده الله إلى جده بيد عدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says a disbeliever took the camel’s reins while the Prophet traveled with Khadīja’s servant Maysara; Gabriel appeared as a man and guided him to the caravan.
rows.anchor: لما خرج مع غلام خديجة ميسرة أخذ كافر بزمام بعيره حتى ضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A separate report says Abū Ṭālib took him toward Syria, lost the road, and God guided him.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن أبا طالب خرج به إلى الشام فضل عن الطريق فهداه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water is called ḍalla when submerged at night; the verse can mean the Prophet was hidden among Meccan unbelievers until God strengthened him to make His religion known.
rows.anchor: يقال : ضل الماء في الليل إذا صار مغمورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs call a solitary tree in open country a lost one; the Prophet was a unique tree bearing faith’s fruit in a barren land, and God guided people through him.
rows.anchor: العرب تسمي الشجرة الفريدة في الفلاة ضالة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The saying that wisdom is the believer’s lost property parallels the unique-tree interpretation.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : «الحكمة ضالة المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a child he lacked knowledge of God; God created in him reason, guidance and knowledge, so ḍāll means lacking knowledge, not holding false belief.
rows.anchor: وجدك ضالا عن معرفة الله تعالى حين كنت طفلا صبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He was unaware of the prophethood he would receive and had no expectation of it; God guided him to a mission Jews and Christians expected only among Israelites.
rows.anchor: كنت ضالا عن النبوة ما كنت تطمع في ذلك ولا خطر شيء من ذلك في قلبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A master may be addressed while the intended referent is his people: they were astray, and God guided them through the Prophet and his law.
rows.anchor: قد يخاطب السيد ،   ويكون المراد قومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may mean he was separate from the astray and distant from their religion; God then guided him to mix with them and call them to the manifest faith.
rows.anchor: وجدك ضالا عن الضالين منفردا عنهم مجانبا لدينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may refer to his uncertainty and wish to leave Quraysh before God authorized emigration; God then guided him to Umm Maʿbad’s tent and the episode of Surāqa.
rows.anchor: وجدك ضالا عن الهجرة ،   متحيرا في يد قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is uncertainty whether the Kaʿba would become his qibla; God guided him toward the qibla he desired.
rows.anchor: كان يتمنى أن تجعل الكعبة قبلة له وما كان يعرف أن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Gabriel first appeared, the Prophet did not know who he was and was terrified; God guided him until he recognized Gabriel.
rows.anchor: حين ظهرها له جبريل عليه السلام في أول أمره ما كان يعرف أهو جبريل أم لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍalāl can mean love, as in Jacob’s love for Joseph; the Prophet was a lover whom God guided to laws by which he could serve his Beloved.
rows.anchor: الضلال بمعنى المحبة كما في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may mean he lacked worldly and commercial knowledge; God guided him to profitable trade, and Khadīja consequently desired him.
rows.anchor: ضالا عن أمور الدنيا لا تعرف التجارة ونحوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He was powerless and mistreated among his people, who would not accept him as a subordinate; God strengthened him until he became their commander.
rows.anchor: فقوي أمرك وهداك إلى أن صرت آمرا واليا عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He did not know the paths of the heavens until God guided him by taking him up on the night journey.
rows.anchor: كنت ضالا ما كنت تهتدي على طريق السموات فهديتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍalāl may mean forgetfulness; awe on the night journey made him forget the praise due, and God taught him to say he could not enumerate His praise.
rows.anchor: نسي ما يجب أن يقال بسبب الهيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although he knew God inwardly, he did not openly display opposition to his people, and this outward stance was called ḍalāl.
rows.anchor: وإن كان عارفا بالله بقلبه إلا أنه كان في الظاهر لا يظهر لهم خلافا

rows.speaker: علي عليه السلام
rows.claim: ʿAlī reports the Prophet’s account that God blocked two youthful intentions to join Meccan entertainments by making him sleep until sunrise; after those occasions he intended no evil until receiving the message.
rows.anchor: روى علي عليه السلام عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : «ما هممت بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀʾil means one burdened with dependents; it is also used for a poor person without dependents.
rows.anchor: ثم أطلق العائل على الفقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The famous interpretation takes ʿāʾil to mean poor or needy.
rows.anchor: وهو المشهور أن المراد هو الفقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s codex reportedly reads ʿadīman, and another reading has ʿayilan.
rows.anchor: في مصحف عبد الله : ( ووجدك عديما ) وقرئ عيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Provision came through Abū Ṭālib’s care, Khadīja’s wealth, Abū Bakr’s wealth, the Anṣār’s aid after emigration and finally booty; later booty counts as realized because its arrival was certain.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى أغناه بتربية أبي طالب

rows.speaker: الصديق
rows.claim: The Prophet worried that spending Khadīja’s money during famine would exhaust it, while withholding it might displease God; she invited Quraysh, and al-Ṣiddīq offered the money for him to use or keep.
rows.anchor: قال الصديق : فأخرجت دنانير وصبتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enriched him through companions who worshipped secretly, ʿUmar’s conversion and confidence, and Abū Bakr’s wealth.
rows.anchor: أغناه بأصحابه كانوا يعبدون الله سرا

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: When he accepted Islam, ʿUmar challenged the secrecy of Muslim worship and urged them to worship openly as others did al-Lāt.
rows.anchor: عمر حين أسلم : أبرز أتعبد اللات جهرا ونعبد الله سرا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said to wait until Muslims had more companions; ʿUmar replied that God and he sufficed, and a verse about God and the believers sufficing is cited.
rows.anchor: عليه السلام :  " حتى تكثر الأصحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He was enriched through contentment, with gold and stone alike and his heart attached only to God; true wealth is needlessness from things, not possession of them.
rows.anchor: أغناك بالقناعة فصرت بحال يستوي عندك الحجر والذهب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Rāzī adds that the Prophet was offered wealth or poverty and chose poverty.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه السلام خير بين الغنى والفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He lacked proofs and arguments until God sent the Qurʾān and taught him what he did not know.
rows.anchor: كنت عائلا عن البراهين والحجج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes his dependents as his community: God sufficed for them through him, since their poverty was ignorance and he had knowledge to guide them.
rows.anchor: في تفسير العائل : أنت كنت كثير العيال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Orphanhood taught the Prophet the worth and needs of orphans; Joseph did not eat his fill lest he forget the hungry.
rows.anchor: أن يعرف قدر اليتامى فيقوم بحقهم وصلاح أمرهم

rows.speaker: يوسف عليه السلام
rows.claim: Joseph explained that he feared eating his fill would make him forget the hungry.
rows.anchor: كان يوسف عليه السلام لا يشبع .   فقيل له في ذلك : فقال أخاف أن أشبع فأنسى الجياع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An orphan shares the Prophet’s designation and should therefore be honored; a report urges honoring and making room for a child named Muḥammad.
rows.anchor: ليكون اليتيم مشاركا له في الاسم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says a child named Muḥammad should be honored and given room in the gathering.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام :  " إذا سميتم الولد محمدا فأكرموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without parents to rely on, he depended on God alone; Rāzī compares this to Abraham’s trust and Mary’s answer that her provision came from God.
rows.anchor: من كان له أب أو أم كان اعتماده عليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since an orphan’s flaws are exposed and may be exaggerated, orphanhood made everyone scrutinize the Prophet; finding no fault left no objection to his appointment.
rows.anchor: أن العادة جارية بأن اليتيم لا تخفى عيوبه بل تظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Orphanhood showed that the Prophet’s excellence came directly from God, since parents can teach and discipline a child.
rows.anchor: جعله يتيما ليعلم كل أحد أن فضيلته من الله ابتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Orphanhood and poverty are disadvantages among people; his supreme rank despite both reverses expectations and is miraculous.
rows.anchor: أن اليتم والفقر نقص في حق الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the favors keeps the Prophet mindful of dependence and prevents self-admiration.
rows.anchor: الحكمة أن لا ينسى نفسه فيقع في العجب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report has the Prophet ask for privileges given to Abraham, Moses, David and Solomon; God recalls these favors, opening his breast, raising his mention, removing his burden, giving him al-Baqara’s closing verses, and offering friendship as with Abraham.
rows.anchor: سألت ربي مسألة وددت أني لم أسألها

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī objects that prophets would not ask this without permission, so the report cannot plausibly portray the Prophet asking and God responding with a reprimand.
rows.anchor: طعن القاضي في هذا الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān means humankind as a kind; taqwīm is shaping a thing as it should be, through proper composition and proportion.
rows.anchor: المراد من الإنسان هذه الماهية والتقويم تصبير الشيء على ما ينبغي أن يكون في التألف والتعديل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that other living creatures are face-down, while humans stand upright and take food with their hands; this concerns outward form.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى خلق كل ذي روح مكبا على وجهه إلا الإنسان فإنه تعالى خلقه مديد القامة يتناول مأكوله بيده

rows.speaker: الأصم
rows.claim: Al-Aṣamm interprets the best proportion as complete intellect, understanding, manners, knowledge and eloquence, addressing inner character rather than outward form.
rows.anchor: الأصم : في أكمل عقل وفهم وأدب وعلم وبيان

rows.speaker: يحيى بن أكثم
rows.claim: Yaḥyā b. Aktham interprets taqwīm as beauty of form; in a moonlit conditional divorce case, he alone ruled that the husband had not broken his oath, citing this verse.
rows.anchor: يحيى بن أكثم القاضي أنه فسر التقويم بحسن الصورة

rows.speaker: يحيى بن أكثم
rows.claim: All jurists but Yaḥyā b. Aktham ruled that the husband had broken his oath; Yaḥyā said he had not.
rows.anchor: إلا يحيى بن أكثم فإنه قال : لا يحنث

rows.speaker: بعض الصالحين
rows.claim: A pious person prays that God who gave humans their best forms in this world will give them their best deeds in the next: pardon and overlooking faults.
rows.anchor: بعض الصالحين يقول : إلهنا أعطيتنا في الأولى

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators say Sūrat al-ʿAlaq was the first revelation.
rows.anchor: زعم المفسرون : أن هذه السورة أول ما نزل من القرآن

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others say al-Fātiḥa was revealed first, followed by Sūrat al-ʿAlaq.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : الفاتحة أول ما نزل ثم سورة العلق

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats the bāʾ as extra, making the command mean to recite or mention the Lord’s name.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : الباء زائدة

rows.speaker: الأخطل
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda adduces al-Akhṭal’s line about women who do not recite sūras as evidence for this sense.
rows.anchor: كما قال الأخطل : هن الحرائر لا ربات أخمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī rejects the analysis: it makes the Prophet’s reply that he cannot read incoherent, commands what he was already constantly doing, and discards the bāʾ without benefit.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول ضعيف لوجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī prefers reading the command as reciting the Qurʾān, since unqualified recitation is used for it, as in verses about its recitation and gradual revelation.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني : أن المراد من قوله : { اقرأ } أي اقرأ القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one analysis, bi-smi rabbika is circumstantial: recite the Qurʾān while beginning with the Lord’s name, saying the basmala first.
rows.anchor: أن يكون محل باسم ربك النصب على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī takes this analysis to show that the basmala must be recited at each sūra’s start, rebutting those who do not deem it obligatory.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أنه يجب قراءة التسمية في ابتداء كل سورة كما أنزل الله تعالى وأمر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is to recite the Qurʾān seeking help through God’s name, an instrument for the difficult task like a pen.
rows.anchor: يكون المعنى اقرأ القرآن مستعينا باسم ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is to perform the act for God and dedicate it to Him; what is devoted to God is beyond Satan’s interference.
rows.anchor: أي اجعل هذا الفعل لله وافعله لأجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning God before a permissible act can figuratively attribute it to Him and protect it from Satan, who shares food when God’s name is omitted.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك إضافة مجازية كما تضيف ضيعتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A permissible act may be dedicated to God when it helps one obey Him, turning it into worship.
rows.anchor: أنه ربما استعان بذلك المباح على التقوى على طاعة الله فيصير المباح طاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Allāh is nobler as a name of the divine essence than rabb, worship is urged effectively through God’s active relation as Lord, which makes it incumbent.
rows.anchor: وهو أن الرب من صفات الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because this was among the first revelations and the Prophet was frightened, rabb reassures him: the One who raised him will not abandon him; beginning care entails completion.
rows.anchor: قد فزع فاستماله ليزول الفزع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī contrasts God’s adding Himself to the Prophet through lordship with describing the Prophet as His servant in the night journey, and cites a saying that ʿAlī and the Prophet belong to one another.
rows.anchor: تارة يضيف ذاته إليه بالربوبية كما ههنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciprocal relation is supported by the declaration that obeying the Messenger is obedience to God.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى : { من يطع الرسول فقد أطاع الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says I am yours rather than you are Mine because benefit has so far flowed from Him to the servant; after obedience or repentance He calls the servant His own.
rows.anchor: فيقول الرب تعالى : المنفعة تصل مني إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once the servant obeys or repents, God adds him to Himself, as in the address to His servants who have wronged themselves.
rows.anchor: أضفتك إلى نفسي فقلت : أنزل على عبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase answers how God is the Prophet’s Lord: he and his attributes were once nonexistent and require a creator; bringing him into existence is nurture and establishes God as Lord.
rows.anchor: لأنك كنت بذاتك وصفاتك معدوما
